messages:
alex: Quick follow-up to the sidecar vs relay RFC — specifically around the handshake and fallback semantics for Private/VPC control plane. Proposal: prefer a persistent per-tenant sidecar tunnel (mTLS) with deterministic IP preservation; on health degradation transition to regional relay fallback for burst/maintenance. Looking for tradeoffs and rollout checklist.

maria: +1 on preserving customer egress IP where possible. main concerns: cost (lots of tunnels) and route table churn if we do per-tenant NAT. can we share a small pool of sidecars per-account? :thinking_face:

tony: If we share sidecars across tenants we lose per-tenant egress IP preservation unless we do SNAT mapping per-connection. That adds hairpin/NAT complexity. Also worried about conn tracking limits on the sidecars.

sophie: We did a spike for ephemeral vs persistent earlier — persistent tunnels simplify KV cache locality and reduce cold-start latency for chat continuations. fallback state machine I used in the spike: CONNECTED -> DEGRADED (packet loss / high RTT) -> FALLBACK (relay active, drain) -> RECONNECT. We should define clear SLO triggers (p50/p95 RTT, 5xx rate) and a drain timeout.

alex: Drafted a simple state table for the agent to implement. quick snippet:

```
# agent handshake states
STATE_CONNECTED: accept requests, advertise local egress-ip
STATE_DEGRADED: start health probe duplication to relay
STATE_FALLBACK: mark tunnel read-only, switch writes to relay, announce relay-route
STATE_RECONNECT: attempt mTLS re-init with backoff
```

alex: Questions: 1) how long do we accept traffic on a degraded tunnel before failing to relay? 2) should we prefer regional relay with sticky session to avoid re-auth for long tail requests? 3) ops: what metrics/logs do we need to unblock debugging?

maria: For 1) my vote: 5s aggressive for LLM inference tail requests, 30s for background control messages (webhooks, config). For 2) yes prefer sticky session for the same request-id to avoid replays.

tony: Metrics: cp.tunnel.latency, cp.tunnel.packet_loss, cp.tunnel.state_transitions, cp.relay.requests_received, cp.relay.route_announcements. Also surface per-tenant conntrack usage and SNAT table size.

sophie: Security: every agent cert rotation must be auditable and short-lived. use per-agent cert signed by private CA and rotate with TTL ~24h by default. fallback relay should reject any requests without valid tenant attestation header to avoid impersonation. @security FYI.

infra-bot: Deploy plan: canary rollout to 10 dedicated tenants (non-SLA), monitor cp.tunnel.state_transitions and cp.relay.fallback_rate for 48h, then 5% of traffic, then 25%, full. Automatic rollback if fallback_rate > 0.5% or error budget burn > 5%.

alex: ops checklist idea: pre-seed relay route announcements, provide a one-click cutover command, and ensure DNS TTLs are low for faster switchover. also add a pairing tool to map tenant -> active-egress-ip for support.

maria: Implementation note: for cost the hybrid option (per-tenant ephemeral sidecar only for heavy tenants, shared sidecars for small tenants) seems best. small-tenants: use regional relay by default, heavy tenants: persistent sidecar.

tony: Agree. Also recommend conntrack tuning on the sidecar and an LRU eviction for per-tenant NAT mappings to avoid DoS from unexpected spikes.

sophie: I'll open a follow-up RFC with the state machine, SLO trigger table, cert rotation flow, and a sample agent config. sample agent config below: 

```
agent:
  sidecar_mode: persistent
  cert_ttl: 24h
  health_probe_interval: 2s
  degraded_threshold: 3 consecutive failed probes
  fallback_grace_seconds: 5
  relay_preference: regional_sticky
```

alex: Perfect — thanks. If nobody objects I'll land the spike docs and a small RFC for the rollout plan. tagging @sre and @security for final sign-off. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Note: created ticket INFRA-4621 to track canary and metrics dashboards.
